title: UniFi device won't adopt to Dream Machine
shortDescription: A UniFi access point or switch cannot be taken over by the controller.
fullDescription:
Adoption brings a UniFi device under the management of a controller (UDM / UniFi Network application). Adoption fails when the device can't reach the inform URL, is still linked to a previous controller, or has a firmware mismatch.

The UniFi UI typically shows 'Adoption Failed' or 'Managed by Other'.

causes.cause: Device still adopted by prior controller

fixSteps.title: Factory reset device
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the reset pin for 10 seconds until LEDs flash. Device will reappear as 'Pending Adoption'.

fixSteps.title: SSH forget
fixSteps.instruction: SSH to device as 'ubnt' (default pw 'ubnt'), run 'set-default' to wipe prior controller lock.

fixSteps.title: Upgrade firmware first
fixSteps.instruction: SSH run 'upgrade <URL>' to match controller's expected version before adopting.

whenToCallPro: Hire a UniFi integrator for multi-site controller migration.

faq.q: What is the default SSH password?
faq.a: ubnt/ubnt for un-adopted devices; current controller credentials after adoption.

title: UDM firmware upgrade stuck pending
shortDescription: Firmware upgrade is downloaded but never applies.
fullDescription: The Dream Machine queues upgrades but sometimes fails to install due to low free storage, an in-progress backup, or a hung UniFi OS service. The UI shows 'Pending' indefinitely.

fixSteps.title: Reboot UDM
fixSteps.instruction: UniFi OS > Console > Restart, or power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Manual upgrade
fixSteps.instruction: Upload firmware file via UniFi OS > Console > Update > Manual install.

fixSteps.title: SSH upgrade
fixSteps.instruction: SSH to UDM and run 'ubnt-systool fwupdate <url>' for specific firmware URL.

whenToCallPro: Call a UniFi pro for production networks to avoid downtime.

faq.a: Yes via manual install, but configs may not restore cleanly across major versions.

title: UniFi device not appearing in controller
shortDescription: Devices don't show up in the 'Pending Adoption' list.
fullDescription: Discovery uses L2 broadcast and DNS unifi.local by default. VLAN separation, broadcast-blocking switches, or missing DHCP option 43 will prevent discovery.

causes.cause: No DHCP option 43 for L3 discovery

symptoms: Device powers up but never lists

fixSteps.title: Put device on mgmt subnet
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily connect to same VLAN as UDM.

fixSteps.title: Add DHCP option 43
fixSteps.instruction: Configure DHCP option 43 hex with controller IP for cross-subnet discovery.

whenToCallPro: Hire a network engineer for L3-discovery setups.

faq.a: L2 broadcast UDP 10001; DHCP option 43 for L3 fallback.

title: Cannot SSH into UDM or managed device
shortDescription: SSH refuses login or is disabled.
fullDescription: SSH on UniFi needs a Device Authentication credential set in UniFi OS. On newer UDM firmware root SSH is locked, and you must use 'root' user with password from OS > Advanced > SSH.

fixSteps.title: Enable SSH and set creds
fixSteps.instruction: UniFi OS > Console > Advanced > SSH > enable and set username/password.

fixSteps.title: Use correct account
fixSteps.instruction: On UDM, SSH with 'root' and the SSH password, not your UniFi UI password.

fixSteps.title: Check firewall
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure WAN rule isn't blocking mgmt SSH; prefer LAN-only access.

whenToCallPro: Engage UniFi partner for key-based auth or MFA setups.

faq.a: Yes, add keys in UniFi OS Advanced > SSH.

title: UDM WAN has no link or no IP
shortDescription: Primary WAN interface is down or fails to obtain an IP.
fullDescription: If the UDM can't acquire a WAN IP, all internal clients lose internet. Commonly caused by wrong WAN mode (DHCP/PPPoE), bad SFP+, or an ISP MAC binding.

causes.cause: ISP MAC binding to previous router

fixSteps.title: Verify WAN mode
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Internet > WAN and set DHCP or PPPoE per ISP.

fixSteps.title: Clone MAC
fixSteps.instruction: If ISP is binding MAC, enable 'Clone MAC' or request reprovision.

fixSteps.title: Swap cable/SFP
fixSteps.instruction: Try a known-good Ethernet/SFP+ to rule out hardware.

whenToCallPro: ISP for MAC reprovision; pro for fiber/SFP+ issues.

faq.a: Settings > Internet > WAN > MAC Address > Clone.

title: UDM CPU pegged near 100%
shortDescription: Controller and routing slow due to CPU saturation.
fullDescription: Heavy DPI, IDS/IPS, and many VPN tunnels can saturate UDM CPU, degrading throughput. Smart Queues + IDS on a gigabit line often exceeds base UDM limits.

fixSteps.title: Limit Smart Queues
fixSteps.instruction: Set Smart Queues to realistic throughput matching CPU capacity.

fixSteps.title: Upgrade hardware
fixSteps.instruction: Move to UDM Pro / SE for gigabit+ with IDS.

whenToCallPro: Network pro for hardware upgrade and migration.

faq.a: Yes – approx 850 Mbps on UDM Pro with IDS on.

title: Site-to-site or client VPN won't connect
shortDescription: Users can't establish VPN tunnels through UDM.
fullDescription: VPN failures are often port-forwarding, mismatched pre-shared keys, or dynamic DNS not resolving. WireGuard (Teleport) issues are usually identity-related.

fixSteps.title: Verify PSK
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm identical PSK on both sides, regenerate if unsure.

fixSteps.title: Check DDNS
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Internet > Dynamic DNS – test resolve from external network.

fixSteps.title: Test port open
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm UDP 500/4500 forwarded and ISP not CG-NAT.

whenToCallPro: Network pro for CG-NAT workarounds and site-to-site troubleshooting.

faq.a: Yes via Teleport and WireGuard VPN server in UniFi Network 7+.

title: UniFi UI can't reach controller
shortDescription: UniFi OS web UI times out or remote cloud access fails.
fullDescription: Controller unreachable can be local (service crashed) or remote (ui.com portal cannot reach device). Checking local LAN first isolates the cause.

fixSteps.title: Try local IP first
fixSteps.instruction: https://<udm-lan-ip> to rule out remote issue.

fixSteps.title: Reboot UDM
fixSteps.instruction: Reboot from UniFi OS or power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Check status.ui.com
fixSteps.instruction: Verify Ubiquiti cloud services are healthy.

whenToCallPro: Pro for persistent controller crashes or DB corruption.

faq.a: Yes – local IP access works without the cloud.

title: UDM Pro/SE PoE budget exceeded
shortDescription: Some PoE ports turn off due to over-budget
fullDescription: UDM SE provides PoE on all 8 LAN ports with a budget of 180W. Overloading triggers a shutdown of the lowest priority ports.

fixSteps.title: Sum PoE wattage
fixSteps.instruction: Check each connected AP/camera and add wattage; stay under 180W.

fixSteps.title: Offload to PoE switch
fixSteps.instruction: Move some PoE devices to a dedicated PoE switch.

whenToCallPro: Low-voltage installer for structured cabling upgrades.

title: UDM config restore doesn't complete
shortDescription: Restoring a backup to UDM fails or rolls back.
fullDescription: Restore errors out when the backup was made on a newer UniFi version than the target, or when hardware model differs. Restoring from UDM Pro backup onto UDM base won't work.

fixSteps.title: Match firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Upgrade target UDM to the same version as backup source before restore.

fixSteps.title: Use same model
fixSteps.instruction: Restore to identical model; cross-model migration requires manual export of settings.

fixSteps.title: Redownload backup
fixSteps.instruction: If file corrupt, fetch fresh backup from UI > System > Backups.

faq.q: Can I restore UDM backup to UDM Pro?
faq.a: Not directly; you need manual settings migration.

title: Adoption failed
fullDescription: UniFi controller cannot adopt device. Common diagnostic indication on Ubiquiti enterprise router. Most issues resolve with reset, firmware update, or hardware swap.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Check for and install latest firmware via app or web UI.

fixSteps.title: Factory reset if needed
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, factory-reset and reconfigure.

whenToCallPro: If reset and firmware update don't resolve, contact support.

faq.a: Often yes — power-cycling resolves transient errors.
Yes, but don't interrupt power during update.
